findings.title: Expected provider failure now logs a full traceback, duplicating the adjacent warning
findings.description:
In `ReviewAction._run_part`, the `except ProviderError as exc:` block now ends with `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error in step %s", context.step_name)` before building the failure result. Two problems, both verifiable in the same block:

1. The message calls this an "unexpected error", but the comment three lines above states the opposite ("a provider failure that leaves nothing on disk erases the only evidence of why the step failed (#84)"). `ProviderError` here is the explicitly expected case, and `_logger.exception` emits a traceback at ERROR for it. That is the convention `DispatchAction._provider_failure` in `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py` deliberately avoids for the same exception class ("A named provider failure (issue 200): the message says what happened, so one ERROR line and no traceback").
2. The block already logs a `_logger.warning("review: provider failed in step %s; failure artifact: %s", ...)` a few lines earlier, so one event now produces two records, one of them with a traceback — which is exactly the noise the issue-200 convention exists to suppress in an unattended run.

`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py`'s `_exception_result` already records the failure into the artifact, and the warning names the artifact path, so the `_logger.exception` line adds nothing but traceback volume. Remove it (or demote it to a `_logger.warning` that does not claim the error was unexpected).

findings.title: `sq stats reviews` raises on an artifact it claims to count as skipped
findings.description:
`reviews_usage_report` documents `skipped` as "unreadable frontmatter" and logs `"skipping review artifact with no readable frontmatter: %s"`, but it only handles the case where `read_frontmatter` returns `None`. `read_frontmatter` in `src/squadron/documents/frontmatter.py` starts with `text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` with no guard, so an artifact that exists but cannot be decoded (`UnicodeDecodeError`) or read (`OSError`) propagates straight out of `reviews_usage_report`. The CLI call site in `src/squadron/cli/commands/stats.py#stats_reviews` has no `try`/`except` either, so `sq stats reviews` tracebacks instead of reporting the artifact as skipped.

This is the asymmetry the module is trying to avoid: `run_usage_report` in `src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py` carefully wraps `state_manager.load` in `except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError, SchemaVersionError)` and raises a named `RunUsageLoadError`, while the reviews path — which walks a directory the user also writes to — has no equivalent. Catch `OSError`/`UnicodeDecodeError` around the `read_frontmatter(path)` call and increment `skipped`, matching the documented contract. A test with a non-UTF-8 `.md` in the directory would pin it.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews` anchors the reviews directory at the process cwd, not the repo root
findings.description:
`reviews_dir = Path.cwd() / REVIEWS_DIR` resolves `project-documents/user/reviews` relative to wherever the command was invoked. Every other review-reading path anchors at the git root instead: `_resolve_review_cwd` in `src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py` calls `resolve_repo_cwd(cwd)`, whose docstring records that this is deliberate ("the git root is the anchor (issue #86)"). Running `sq stats reviews` from `src/`, a worktree subdirectory, or any nested path therefore reports "No review directory at …/src/project-documents/user/reviews" and exits 0 — a silent empty answer for a read-only reporting command, which is the failure mode issue #86 already fixed once for `sq review`.

Resolve the directory through the same helper the review commands use (accepting a `--cwd` override, as `sq review` does) so the two surfaces cannot disagree about where reviews live.

findings.title: `--json` on the missing-directory path emits plain text, not JSON
findings.description:
In `stats_reviews`, the `report.missing_dir` early return happens *before* the `as_json` branch, so `sq stats reviews --json` from a directory with no reviews writes `No review directory at /path` to stdout and exits 0. A consumer doing `sq stats reviews --json | jq` gets a parse error rather than an empty result. The flag's contract — stated in its own help text as "Emit the rows and totals as JSON" — is broken on exactly the path a scripted caller is most likely to hit (a fresh checkout, a CI job, a repo with no reviews yet).

Either emit the JSON envelope with `"rows": []` and `"missing_dir": true`, or send the human-readable message to stderr (`typer.echo(..., err=True)`) so stdout stays machine-parseable — the pattern `sq review` already uses via `_report_console(json_stdout)`. Note `stats_run` already routes its error through `err=True`, so the two subcommands of the same app currently disagree.

findings.title: `get_all_aliases()` is uncached and the new code calls it once per row and a fourth time per resolution
findings.description:
`get_all_aliases()` re-reads and re-parses two TOML files on every call:

```python
merged = load_builtin_aliases()   # is_file() + read_text() + tomllib.loads()
merged.update(load_user_aliases())  # same, for ~/.config/squadron/models.toml
```

There is no cache — a grep for `lru_cache`/`functools.cache` across `src/` finds only `src/squadron/review/parsers.py:713`. This slice adds three new call sites on paths that run per item:

- `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py#_record` calls it once per review artifact, so `sq stats reviews` over a repo with a few hundred reviews performs a few hundred redundant file reads plus TOML parses.
- `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py#_is_subscription` calls it once per rendered row via `cost_cell`.
- `src/squadron/pipeline/resolver.py#_resolved` adds a fourth call per model resolution (`model_allows_tools`, `model_max_output_tokens`, and `model_effort` each already call it), and `_resolved` runs per step, per fan-out branch, and per pool selection.

`get_all_aliases()` is a pure read of on-disk configuration within a process, so caching it (with an explicit invalidation point for config reload, or a `lru_cache` keyed on the two paths' mtimes) removes the repetition without changing behavior. At minimum, hoist the lookup out of the per-row loops in the two new stats modules.

findings.title: `effort_for_session` is named and used as a getter but always returns `None`
findings.description:
The method is annotated `-> None` and its body only emits a one-time DEBUG line; the "effort the SDK session path sends" is, by design, always `None` (D7, #216). But `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py#_dispatch_via_session` and `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/summary.py#_execute_summary` both write `effort_sent = capture.effort_for_session(resolved)` and then pass `effort_sent=effort_sent` into `record_from_telemetry`, which reads as though the value were the measured effort. The docstring's own summary sentence ("The effort the SDK session path sends: none") is at least self-contradicting: it returns nothing.

Renaming it to something that describes the side effect (`note_session_effort_gap`, `log_effort_not_applied`) would make the call sites honest; passing a literal `effort_sent=None` beside it would make the record's meaning unmistakable.

findings.title: The totals denominator counts only LLM actions while `priced` counts every record
findings.description:
`_total_row` renders `f"{format_usd(totals.cost_usd)} ({totals.priced} of {actions} priced)"`, where `render_run_report` passes `actions=report.llm_actions` and `report.llm_actions` filters on `LLM_ACTION_TYPES` (`src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py`). `UsageTotals.priced`, however, is incremented in `usage_totals` for *every* record with a `cost_usd`, with no action-type filter — unlike its sibling `RunUsageReport.unrecorded`, which does apply the filter.

The invariant that keeps `priced <= actions` today holds only by convention: no non-LLM action currently stamps a usage record. A future `cf-op` or `commit` action that records anything would make the row read `(3 of 2 priced)`. Applying the same `LLM_ACTION_TYPES` filter to `priced` (or documenting why the two counts intentionally use different populations) removes the latent contradiction between two properties of the same report object.
